column1: # The latest independent audit of each table: an auditor who did not write the entries drew a random sample of rows graded understood
# and re-derived each from the binaries or the cited specification. real = the entry held up, shallow = true but derived from a name or
# credited without behaviour of its own, wrong = contradicted. sample is small: read it with the percentage. The last row of a table with
# the latest date is the one summary.tsv and docs/coverage.md show.

column7: sample of the routine rows and second-bank copies added since the seed review (seed 20261102); each disassembled from the 1.44.0 Origin 300 body and the relocated copies compared byte for byte; every claimed argument, call, store and literal held
general_req_war_flag in the 2 MB package and the L2 partition task's brick lookup, both read from the handler through the flag or database call to the reply record
the chip-select 3 control write of the USB slot setup: value, address and offset read in the image, register name checked against the public chip map
the Linux L1 package of 1.44.0: kernel release and every cramfs entry count re-derived by walking the image (both Linux packages agree)

the on-chip peripherals note and the USB controller register note held; the 2 MB package comparison said the request task initialiser differs between the 1 MB and 2 MB packages when the pairing had split one routine (package 1 has the same guard, semaphore and registration); corrected

twenty of the 25 open-question entries drawn at random and re-derived from the image and the carved L2 tree: addresses, counts, callers and string literals held for 17; three were shallow (the USB part route pointed at a host-side driver that cannot name controller silicon, the routine at 0xffe48370 is a 28-byte wrapper and the entry asked to read it, and the writers of settings 9 and 0x10 were already locatable); the guard-word entry put the peer initializer's entry at the wrong address; fixed

twenty of the 636 rows of the two L1 request tables drawn at random (seed 20261102; ten per table); each code-to-handler address re-derived by tracing the compare chain with a separate interpreter and each text claim by re-decoding the handler with its own bounds (all addresses, line counts and same, RAM-only or changed classifications held); three were shallow because the compared text is only a short setup stub that branches into shared code, which the page caveated for one code in one set only; the page now says so for every set
